iterations.theme: Cameron Macgregor o ratu u Iranu: Trumpova dilema, pad američke moći, globalne ekonomske posljedice i duhovna obnova Zapada

sections.subtitle: Podcast Mrežnica preko Atlantika: gost koji je bio i u Hrvatskoj
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pozdravlja gosta Camerona Macgregora na početku razgovora
sections.content:
Nakon duže stanke podcast **Mrežnica** ponovno prelazi Atlantski ocean. Ovaj put odredište su Sjedinjene Američke Države, a sugovornik je **Cameron Macgregor**. Voditelj ga predstavlja kao iznimno dobrog poznavatelja ekonomije i geopolitike, YouTubera i svjetskog putnika. Najavljuje i da je Macgregor bio u Hrvatskoj, ali tu priču ostavlja za sam kraj razgovora.

Voditelj odmah otkriva okvir razgovora. Tema su stanje u Sjedinjenim Državama, gostov pogled na rat s Iranom, odnosno u Iranu, te ekonomska budućnost koja, kako kaže, „svima nama ne izgleda baš ružičasto“.

Razgovor počinje srdačno. Macgregor voditelja pozdravlja s „Dobro večer“ na hrvatskom, ali odmah priznaje da zna tek nekoliko fraza. Voditelj zato predlaže da nastave na engleskom.
sections.subtitle_en: Podcast Mrežnica Across the Atlantic: A Guest Who Has Also Been to Croatia
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host greets the guest Cameron Macgregor at the beginning of the conversation
sections.content_en:
After a long break, the podcast **Mrežnica** is once again crossing the Atlantic Ocean. This time the destination is the United States of America, and the interlocutor is **Cameron Macgregor**. The host introduces him as an exceptionally good connoisseur of economics and geopolitics, a YouTuber, and a world traveler. He also announces that Macgregor has been to Croatia, but leaves that story for the very end of the conversation.

The host immediately reveals the framework of the conversation. The topics are the situation in the United States, the guest's view of the war with Iran, that is, in Iran, and the economic future that, as he says, "does not look very rosy to all of us."

The conversation begins warmly. Macgregor greets the host with "Dobro večer" in Croatian, but immediately admits that he knows only a few phrases. The host therefore suggests that they continue in English.

sections.subtitle: Rat bez američkih interesa i bez jasne strategije
sections.screenshot_description: Cameron Macgregor objašnjava zašto je, po njegovu mišljenju, rat u Iranu uopće započeo
sections.content:
Voditelj pita što je rat u Iranu dosad donio. Macgregor najprije želi razjasniti nekoliko stvari koje smatra ključnima, a prva je pitanje zašto se rat uopće dogodio. Ratovi su inače složeni pothvati, objašnjava, iza kojih stoje ekonomski razlozi, političke motivacije i katkad vojno-strateški izračuni.

Za ovaj rat nudi jednostavnije i oštrije objašnjenje. Tvrdi da je **Donald Trump obećao voditi ovaj rat** i da je to bio jedan od preduvjeta njegova izbora na jesen 2024. Obećanje je, prema Macgregoru, dao Američko-izraelskom odboru za javne poslove (American Israel Public Affairs Committee) i drugim interesnim skupinama u SAD-u. Za te skupine kaže da su „preuzele potpunu kontrolu nad američkom vladom“.

Macgregor naglašava da rat nije posljedica američkih nacionalnih interesa. Po njegovim riječima, u ovom sukobu nijedan američki nacionalni interes nije u pitanju, a rat im čak izravno proturječi.

Druga poanta odnosi se na strategiju. Ako SAD nije ušao u rat zbog svojih interesa, pita se gost, koja je onda strategija? Odgovara da je zasad ne vidi, osim nejasne zamisli o **promjeni režima**. Ta zamisao, tvrdi, dolazi na poticaj izraelskog premijera i „jastrebovskih“ članova američke vlade koji Iran žele napasti već desetljećima. Rat stoga opisuje kao vrhunac „koktela interesa“ koji namjerno potkopavaju interese Sjedinjenih Država, njihovih građana i, kako dodaje, cijelog svijeta.
sections.subtitle_en: A War Without American Interests and Without a Clear Strategy
sections.screenshot_description_en: Cameron Macgregor explains why, in his opinion, the war in Iran even began
sections.content_en:
The host asks what the war in Iran has brought so far. Macgregor first wants to clarify several things that he considers key, the first of which is the question of why the war even occurred. Wars are otherwise complex undertakings, he explains, behind which lie economic reasons, political motivations, and sometimes military-strategic calculations.

For this war, he offers a simpler and sharper explanation. He claims that **Donald Trump promised to wage this war** and that this was one of the prerequisites for his election in the fall of 2024. The promise, according to Macgregor, was made to the American Israel Public Affairs Committee and other interest groups in the US. About these groups, he says that they have "taken total control of the American government."

Macgregor emphasizes that the war is not a consequence of American national interests. In his words, in this conflict no American national interest is at stake, and the war even directly contradicts them.

The second point relates to strategy. If the US did not enter the war because of its interests, the guest asks, what then is the strategy? He replies that for now he does not see one, except for a vague idea of **regime change**. That idea, he claims, comes at the instigation of the Israeli prime minister and the "hawkish" members of the American government who have wanted to attack Iran for decades. He therefore describes the war as the culmination of a "cocktail of interests" that deliberately undermine the interests of the United States, its citizens, and, as he adds, the entire world.

sections.subtitle: Rat od 72 sata koji se pretvorio u iransku prednost
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje kako je Washington očekivao brz rat koji bi trajao 48 do 72 sata
sections.content:
Prema Macgregoru, predsjednik, njegovi savjetnici u Pentagonu i obavještajne agencije ulazili su u sukob s uvjerenjem da će rat biti **iznimno kratak**. Očekivali su da će završiti za 48 do 72 sata, a najkasnije za tjedan dana.

Takva su očekivanja, objašnjava, počivala na procjeni da je Iran slab. Washington je računao s nekoliko slabosti:

- **krizom vode**,
- **inflacijskom i ekonomskom krizom**,
- **rastućim otporom** diljem zemlje,
- **izolacijom** Irana u regiji.

Otkrili su, kaže gost, upravo suprotno. U sukobu su, po njegovoj ocjeni, u nepovoljnijem položaju SAD i Izrael, a ne Iran. Iran se posljednjih nekoliko desetljeća pripremao vojno i geopolitički. Režim je, tvrdi, toliko ukopan da ga Sjedinjene Države ne mogu iskorijeniti.

Macgregor ističe da je Iran uzvraćao vrlo promišljeno i strateški. Posebno je nanio bol zaljevskim državama zato što su udomile „američki imperijalizam“ i poslovale s Izraelom. Zaključak mu je bez zadrške: rat zasad dobiva Iran, i to, kako kaže, **odlučno**.
sections.subtitle_en: A 72-Hour War That Turned into an Iranian Advantage
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes how Washington expected a fast war lasting 48 to 72 hours
sections.content_en:
According to Macgregor, the president, his advisers in the Pentagon, and intelligence agencies entered the conflict with the conviction that the war would be **exceptionally short**. They expected it to end in 48 to 72 hours, or at the latest in a week.

Such expectations, he explains, rested on the assessment that Iran is weak. Washington counted on several weaknesses:

- **a water crisis**,
- **an inflationary and economic crisis**,
- **growing resistance** across the country,
- **isolation** of Iran in the region.

They discovered, says the guest, precisely the opposite. In the conflict, according to his assessment, the US and Israel are in a more unfavorable position, not Iran. Over the last few decades, Iran has been preparing militarily and geopolitically. The regime, he claims, is so entrenched that the United States cannot eradicate it.

Macgregor points out that Iran retaliated very deliberately and strategically. It especially inflicted pain on the Gulf states because they hosted "American imperialism" and did business with Israel. His conclusion is without hesitation: for now, Iran is winning the war, and that, as he says, **decisively**.

sections.subtitle: Trumpova dilema: eskalacija vodi u gore, povlačenje u poniženje
sections.screenshot_description: Cameron Macgregor opisuje Trumpov izbor između eskalacije i povlačenja
sections.content:
Voditelj pita mogu li se SAD izvući iz rata bez posljedica. Macgregor odgovara kratko: **ne**. Odgovor veže uz Trumpov karakter, o kojem je, kako kaže, nedavno vodio mnogo razgovora.

Trump je, prema gostu, cijelu karijeru i životnu priču izgradio na tome da se nikada ne ispričava i nikada ne priznaje poraz. Od nečega odustaje samo uz marketinški ili narativni zaokret koji ga prikazuje u dobrom svjetlu. Sada ga je, slikovito kaže Macgregor, „svemir suočio sa situacijom u kojoj nema nikakve pobjede“. Ostaje mu izbor između dvije mogućnosti:

- **Eskalacija**: stvari će postati mnogo gore za Sjedinjene Države, globalnu ekonomiju i regiju. Dogodit će se „svakakve loše stvari“, a Trumpova administracija će se na kraju urušiti.
- **Povlačenje**: Trump će biti politički ponižen, Izrael će biti neutraliziran kao velika regionalna sila, a globalna ekonomija pretrpjet će kolateralnu štetu. Ta je ekonomija, prema Macgregoru, ionako na rubu recesije.

Gost dodaje da je energetska kriza neizbježna, ako već nije počela, te da SAD čekaju ozbiljni gubici u opremi i ljudstvu.
sections.subtitle_en: Trump's Dilemma: Escalation Leads to Worse, Withdrawal to Humiliation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Cameron Macgregor describes Trump's choice between escalation and withdrawal
sections.content_en:
The host asks whether the US can extract itself from the war without consequences. Macgregor answers briefly: **no**. He links the answer to Trump's character, about which, as he says, he has recently had many conversations.

Trump, according to the guest, built his entire career and life story on never apologizing and never admitting defeat. He backs down from something only with a marketing or narrative pivot that presents him in a good light. Now, as Macgregor vividly says, "the universe has confronted him with a situation in which there is no victory whatsoever." He is left with a choice between two possibilities:

- **Escalation**: things will become much worse for the United States, the global economy, and the region. "All kinds of bad things" will happen, and the Trump administration will eventually collapse.
- **Withdrawal**: Trump will be politically humiliated, Israel will be neutralized as a major regional power, and the global economy will suffer collateral damage. That economy, according to Macgregor, is already on the verge of recession anyway.

The guest adds that an energy crisis is inevitable, if it has not already begun, and that serious losses in equipment and personnel await the US.

sections.subtitle: Tisuće vojnika bez plana za izvlačenje
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o konferenciji za medije državnog tajnika Marca Rubija i položaju američkih vojnika
sections.content:
Kao potvrdu svoje teze Macgregor navodi konferenciju za medije koju je prethodnog tjedna održao državni tajnik **Marco Rubio**. Opisuje je kao „mučnu“ i kaže da je Rubio kroz nju morao „manevrirati“.

Na toj se konferenciji, prema gostu, pokazalo da SAD trenutačno **nemaju plan** kako s Bliskog istoka izvući tisuće pripadnika vojske i osoblja. Situaciju opisuje kao nesigurnu: Amerikanci, kaže, ne kontroliraju ni nebo ni more.

Zaključak ponavlja kao refren. Trump će u najboljem slučaju izgubiti obraz, a ako ostane na istom kursu, vjerojatno će izgubiti administraciju. „To je ono s čime se suočava“, kaže Macgregor.
sections.subtitle_en: Thousands of Troops Without an Extraction Plan
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest talks about Secretary of State Marco Rubio's press conference and the position of American soldiers
sections.content_en:
As confirmation of his thesis, Macgregor cites the press conference held the previous week by Secretary of State **Marco Rubio**. He describes it as "painful" and says that Rubio had to "maneuver" through it.

At that conference, according to the guest, it was shown that the US currently **has no plan** for how to extract thousands of members of the military and personnel from the Middle East. He describes the situation as precarious: the Americans, he says, control neither the sky nor the sea.

He repeats the conclusion like a refrain. In the best case, Trump will lose face, and if he remains on the same course, he will likely lose his administration. "That is what he is confronted with," Macgregor says.

sections.subtitle: Od obitelji iz 1620. do elita koje ne vide promijenjeni svijet
sections.screenshot_description: Cameron Macgregor govori o obiteljskim korijenima u Novoj Engleskoj i smjeni američkih elita
sections.content:
Voditelj pita kako je Donald Trump postao **ratni predsjednik**. Macgregor kaže da mu je to vrlo tužno pitanje, osobito zbog obiteljske povijesti. Njegova je obitelj stigla u Ameriku 1620., prije nego što su Sjedinjene Države uopće postojale, i iskrcala se u Novoj Engleskoj. Sebe vidi kao dio naraštaja Amerikanaca koji su u Sjevernoj Americi utemeljili civilizaciju. Ona je najprije bila skup slobodnih država, a zatim postala jedna od velikih svjetskih sila.

Otprilike od Drugoga svjetskog rata, a prema nekima od 1960-ih, Macgregor vidi **smjenu elita**. Nove elite smješta uglavnom na Wall Street, ali i u šire područje Washingtona. To su, opisuje, ljudi koji žive od vojno-industrijskog kompleksa, rade u neprofitnim organizacijama i think-tankovima iz kojih se popunjava vlada. Školuju se na Georgetownovoj školi vanjske službe, Sveučilištu Tufts ili Kennedyjevoj školi na Harvardu.

Te su elite, objašnjava gost, odrasle u svijetu u kojem su SAD bile arbitar međunarodnog prava i pravde i određivale ravnotežu moći. Američka ekonomija bila je najvažnija na svijetu, a Washington je smatrao svojom obvezom intervenirati na Bliskom istoku, u Južnoj Aziji i Istočnoj Europi kako bi „policijski nadzirao svijet“.

Taj je svijet, po Macgregoru, **završio prije dvadeset godina**, a sada se to vidi i na vojnom polju. Ljudi koji vode Washington i savjetuju predsjednika, tvrdi, ne shvaćaju da se svijet promijenio.

Drugi problem vidi u utjecaju ljudi kojima nije stalo do američkih nacionalnih interesa. Mnogi od njih su, tvrdi, strani državljani ili iseljenici koji usmjeravaju američku politiku, ne samo na Bliskom istoku nego i u Latinskoj Americi. Oni, kaže, ne stavljaju Ameriku na prvo mjesto niti daju prednost interesima prosječnih Amerikanaca. Time su ugled, interese i resurse zemlje izložili velikoj opasnosti. Trumpov izbor trebao je to promijeniti, ali nije. Prema gostu, samo je učvrstio istu „klikuu interesa“, a Amerika se našla usred „još jednog katastrofalnog rata“.
sections.subtitle_en: From a 1620 Family to Elites Who Do Not See a Changed World
sections.screenshot_description_en: Cameron Macgregor talks about family roots in New England and the changing of American elites
sections.content_en:
The host asks how Donald Trump became a **wartime president**. Macgregor says that for him this is a very sad question, especially because of his family history. His family arrived in America in 1620, before the United States even existed, and landed in New England. He sees himself as part of a generation of Americans who established civilization in North America. It was first a collection of free states, and then became one of the world's great powers.

Roughly since the Second World War, and according to some since the 1960s, Macgregor sees a **changing of elites**. He places the new elites mainly on Wall Street, but also in the wider Washington area. These are, he describes, people who live off the military-industrial complex, work in non-profit organizations and think tanks from which the government is staffed. They are educated at Georgetown's School of Foreign Service, Tufts University, or the Kennedy School at Harvard.

These elites, the guest explains, grew up in a world in which the US was the arbiter of international law and justice and determined the balance of power. The American economy was the most important in the world, and Washington considered it its duty to intervene in the Middle East, South Asia, and Eastern Europe to "police the world."

That world, according to Macgregor, **ended twenty years ago**, and now this is visible on the military battlefield as well. The people who run Washington and advise the president, he claims, do not realize that the world has changed.

He sees another problem in the influence of people who do not care about American national interests. Many of them, he claims, are foreign nationals or expatriates who direct American policy, not only in the Middle East but also in Latin America. They, he says, do not put America first nor do they give priority to the interests of average Americans. Thereby they have exposed the country's reputation, interests, and resources to great danger. Trump's election was supposed to change that, but it did not. According to the guest, it only entrenched the same "clique of interests," and America found itself in the middle of "yet another catastrophic war."

sections.subtitle: Prosječni Amerikanac gleda cijene goriva, a ne Bliski istok
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava da prosječne Amerikance zasad najviše brinu troškovi života
sections.content:
Voditelj pita jesu li prosječni Amerikanci nakon napada na Iran bijesni na predsjednika. Macgregor odgovara: **ne, još ne**. Prosječnog Amerikanca trenutačno više brine rast troškova života, ponajprije cijene namirnica i benzina.

Gost upozorava na nešto što je, kaže, mnogim Europljanima i ljudima diljem svijeta teško shvatiti: SAD su **vrlo izolirane**. Do Europe ili većine drugih dijelova svijeta treba pet do deset sati leta. Zato Amerikanci ne mare previše za zbivanja izvan granica i ne razumiju ih. Znaju samo da ne žele da se njihova zemlja upliće, ni na Bliskom istoku ni u borbe protiv Rusa ili bilo koga drugoga. Takav je stav, ističe, prisutan već dugo. Dosadašnji ratovi ih nisu izravno pogađali, a ovaj put hoće.

Amerikanci još ne znaju što se zaista događa na Bliskom istoku i još vjeruju predsjedniku. Ipak, kako kaže gost, osjećaju da je ovo loša ideja i gledaju kako rastu cijene na benzinskim crpkama.

Ako se rat nastavi tjednima i mjesecima, što Macgregor očekuje, slijedi teži scenarij. Smatra da je ovo tek početak regionalnog i velikog rata u kojem će Amerikanci ginuti, opskrbni lanci će biti ugroženi, a nasilje i razaranje postupno će rasti u regiji neophodnoj globalnoj ekonomiji. Amerikanci će to osjetiti, a to će, tvrdi, **uništiti Trumpovo predsjedništvo**.

Od toga nas dijele tek tjedni, procjenjuje gost, jer su američka ekonomija i financijski sustav krhki i na rubu recesije. Sam skok cijene nafte mogao bi zemlju gurnuti u recesiju, a krivnja bi pala na Trumpa. „Tamo idemo, ali još nismo stigli“, zaključuje.
sections.subtitle_en: The Average American Looks at Fuel Prices, Not the Middle East
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains that for now, average Americans are most worried about the cost of living
sections.content_en:
The host asks whether average Americans, following the attack on Iran, are furious with the president. Macgregor answers: **no, not yet**. The average American is currently more worried about the rising cost of living, primarily the prices of groceries and gasoline.

The guest warns of something that, he says, is hard for many Europeans and people around the world to understand: the US is **very isolated**. It takes a five to ten hour flight to reach Europe or most other parts of the world. That is why Americans do not care too much about events outside their borders and do not understand them. They only know that they do not want their country to get involved, neither in the Middle East nor in fighting against the Russians or anyone else. Such an attitude, he points out, has been present for a long time. Past wars did not affect them directly, but this time it will.

Americans do not yet know what is truly happening in the Middle East and still believe the president. Still, as the guest says, they feel that this is a bad idea and watch prices rise at gas stations.

If the war continues for weeks and months, which Macgregor expects, a harder scenario follows. He considers this to be only the beginning of a regional and major war in which Americans will perish, supply chains will be threatened, and violence and destruction will gradually increase in a region essential to the global economy. Americans will feel this, and that, he claims, will **destroy Trump's presidency**.

We are only weeks away from that, the guest estimates, because the American economy and financial system are fragile and on the verge of recession. A spike in the price of oil alone could push the country into recession, and the blame would fall on Trump. "That is where we are heading, but we have not arrived yet," he concludes.

sections.subtitle: Lekcija iz Ukrajine: Iran kao civilizacijska država
sections.screenshot_description: Cameron Macgregor uspoređuje rat u Ukrajini s ratom u Iranu
sections.content:
Na pitanje tko može donijeti mir na Bliski istok Macgregor priznaje da je to „vrlo trnovito pitanje“. Odgovor započinje usporedbom s ruskom **specijalnom vojnom operacijom u Ukrajini** jer, kaže, izravno objašnjava ono što se događa na Bliskom istoku.

Mnogi eurokrati i tehnokrati u Bruxellesu, kao i ljudi koji vode europske vlade i američka administracija, vjerovali su da je ruska operacija iz 2022. djelo „megalomana Vladimira Putina“, odnosno „luđačke sile“ i autoritarnog režima koji je napao suverenu zemlju. To je, kaže gost, bio službeni narativ, ali se po njemu nije tako dogodilo. Rusija je, objašnjava, **civilizacijska država** koja se osjetila ugroženom zbog širenja NATO-a i gomilanja snaga na svojoj granici. Na Zapadu su mnogi očekivali da će Rusija brzo izgubiti, da će Putinov režim pasti i da će Zapad odlučno pobijediti. To se, napominje, nije dogodilo.

Iran je, nastavlja Macgregor, također civilizacijska država s tisućama godina povijesti i različitim religijama i etničkim skupinama. Vrlo je složena zemlja, veličine Zapadne Europe i s gotovo sto milijuna stanovnika. Za Irance, odnosno Perzijance, ovo je **rat egzistencijalne krize i identiteta**. Operacija promjene režima trebala je trajati tri ili četiri dana, a umjesto toga, kaže gost, „isprovocirali smo cijelu civilizaciju da se brani pod svaku cijenu“.

Zato vjeruje da će rat završiti tek kad se SAD povuku iz regije i kad Izrael bude „vjerojatno neutraliziran“. Na pitanje što to znači priznaje da ne zna. Nada se padu Netanyahuove vlade i dolasku razumnije vlasti, ali ne isključuje ni uništenje Izraela. Bez toga ne vidi kraj rata. Tvrdi da je cijela regija, ne samo Iran, nego i ono što naziva „kućom islama“, zaključila da stabilnosti na Bliskom istoku neće biti dok SAD i Izrael ne budu poraženi.
sections.subtitle_en: A Lesson from Ukraine: Iran as a Civilizational State
sections.screenshot_description_en: Cameron Macgregor compares the war in Ukraine with the war in Iran
sections.content_en:
To the question of who can bring peace to the Middle East, Macgregor admits that this is a "very thorny question." He begins his answer with a comparison to the Russian **special military operation in Ukraine** because, he says, it directly explains what is happening in the Middle East.

Many Eurocrats and technocrats in Brussels, as well as the people who run European governments and the American administration, believed that the 2022 Russian operation was the work of a "megalomaniac Vladimir Putin," that is, a "mad force" and an authoritarian regime that attacked a sovereign country. That, says the guest, was the official narrative, but according to him it did not happen that way. Russia, he explains, is a **civilizational state** that felt threatened by NATO expansion and the buildup of forces on its border. In the West, many expected that Russia would lose quickly, that Putin's regime would fall, and that the West would win decisively. That, he notes, did not happen.

Iran, Macgregor continues, is also a civilizational state with thousands of years of history and diverse religions and ethnic groups. It is a very complex country, the size of Western Europe and with nearly one hundred million inhabitants. For Iranians, or Persians, this is a **war of existential crisis and identity**. The regime change operation was supposed to last three or four days, and instead, the guest says, "we provoked an entire civilization to defend itself at all costs."

Therefore, he believes that the war will end only when the US withdraws from the region and when Israel is "probably neutralized." When asked what that means, he admits that he does not know. He hopes for the fall of Netanyahu's government and the arrival of a more reasonable administration, but he does not rule out the destruction of Israel either. Without that, he sees no end to the war. He claims that the entire region, not only Iran, but also what he calls the "house of Islam," has concluded that there will be no stability in the Middle East until the US and Israel are defeated.

sections.subtitle: Treći svjetski rat? Ne još, ali mina je aktivirana
sections.screenshot_description: Gost odgovara na pitanje jesmo li već u Trećem svjetskom ratu
sections.content:
Voditelj postavlja izravno pitanje: jesmo li već u **Trećem svjetskom ratu**? Macgregor dvaput ponavlja: „Ne još.“ Prema njemu, počeo je regionalni rat, a Iran podupire strateški savez predvođen ponajprije **Kinom i Rusijom**.

Gost upozorava da Kina i Rusija, suprotno uvriježenom mišljenju na Zapadu, ne igraju nekakav geopolitički šah. Rusija je usredotočena na svoje granice, na pobjedu u Ukrajini te na ekonomsku modernizaciju i razvoj, a isto vrijedi i za Kinu. Obje će zato učiniti sve da izbjegnu širenje sukoba, osim ako im se on ne nametne.

Bliski istok je, slikovito kaže Macgregor, oduvijek bio „mina blizine“. Ta je mina sada aktivirana, što znači da će u sukob vjerojatno biti uvučene sve sile u regiji. Što to dugoročno znači za Ruse i Kineze, i moraju li oni ući u rat da bi postao svjetski, „tek ćemo saznati“.

Dobrom viješću smatra to što su Kina i Rusija relativno stabilne i relativno dobro vođene. Njihove ekonomije nisu imune na sukob, ali su poduzele korake da se od njega zaštite.

Svjetski rat se, po gostu, može izbjeći ako dođe do **promjene režima na Zapadu**. Precizira da svijet mora ući u razdoblje nakon EU-a, nakon NATO-a i, kako kaže, u „postcionistički“ svijet u Sjedinjenim Državama. Ako se to dogodi brzo, svjetskog rata neće biti jer će nestati povod za sukob. Otvoreno je, dodaje, koliko će kolateralne štete nastati do tada i koliko će trebati prosječnim Amerikancima, Nijemcima, Francuzima i Englezima da se probude i „izbace svoje vlade“. Na to pitanje odgovora nema: „Ne znam.“
sections.subtitle_en: World War III? Not Yet, but the Mine Has Been Triggered
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest answers the question of whether we are already in World War III
sections.content_en:
The host asks a direct question: are we already in **World War III**? Macgregor repeats twice: "Not yet." According to him, a regional war has begun, and Iran is supported by a strategic alliance led primarily by **China and Russia**.

The guest warns that China and Russia, contrary to popular belief in the West, are not playing some kind of geopolitical chess. Russia is focused on its borders, on victory in Ukraine, and on economic modernization and development, and the same goes for China. Both will therefore do everything to avoid the spread of the conflict, unless it is forced upon them.

The Middle East, Macgregor vividly says, has always been a "proximity mine." That mine has now been triggered, which means that all powers in the region will likely be drawn into the conflict. What this means in the long run for the Russians and the Chinese, and whether they must enter the war for it to become global, "we are yet to find out."

He considers it good news that China and Russia are relatively stable and relatively well managed. Their economies are not immune to the conflict, but they have taken steps to protect themselves from it.

A world war, according to the guest, can be avoided if **regime change in the West** occurs. He specifies that the world must enter a post-EU, post-NATO, and, as he says, "post-Zionist" world in the United States. If that happens quickly, there will be no world war because the cause for conflict will disappear. It remains open, he adds, how much collateral damage will occur until then and how long it will take for average Americans, Germans, Frenchmen, and Englishmen to wake up and "throw out their governments." To that question, there is no answer: "I don't know."

sections.subtitle: Energetska kriza koja pogađa trećinu svjetskog sustava
sections.screenshot_description: Cameron Macgregor objašnjava razmjere globalne energetske krize i ključne pomorske prolaze
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća na vijesti o naglom rastu cijena nafte i plina i pita kakve geopolitičke i ekonomske posljedice treba očekivati. Macgregor posljedice razlaže u tri točke.

**Prva je energetska kriza.** U najmanju ruku, kaže, svijet je u globalnoj energetskoj krizi koja je već počela. Vjeruje da će se vrlo vjerojatno pretvoriti u globalnu recesiju ili depresiju. Posebno ističe ovisnost Azije o protoku ne samo nafte nego i ukapljenog prirodnog plina, petrokemikalija i gnojiva, kao i o globalnoj trgovini. Sav taj promet ne prolazi samo kroz **Hormuški tjesnac** nego i kroz **Sueski kanal**, **Crveno more** i druge uske prolaze uz rub rata koji se širi Bliskim istokom.

Kriza, procjenjuje gost, pogađa između petine i trećine globalnog energetskog sustava i ne može se lako riješiti. Ako rat brzo završi, mogla bi trajati mjesecima, a ako ne završi, godinama.

**Druga točka je krhkost zapadnih ekonomija.** Gospodarstva Zapadne Europe i SAD-a, kaže Macgregor, već balansiraju na rubu velike krize. Pod tim podrazumijeva nekoliko istodobnih kriza:

- **dužničku krizu** u SAD-u i Zapadnoj Europi,
- **krizu troškova života**,
- **slom društvene kohezije**.

Slom kohezije gost pripisuje tome što su zapadne zemlje, kako tvrdi, „preplavljene milijunima ljudi“ koji žive od državne preraspodjele i čiji egzistencijalni minimum subvencioniraju vlade kojima ponestaje novca. Rat će, smatra, tu krhkost ubrzati. Moguća je financijska kriza, a zatim i svojevrsna ekonomska depresija u Zapadnoj Europi i SAD-u. Može se reći, dodaje, da je taj proces već počeo.
sections.subtitle_en: An Energy Crisis Affecting a Third of the Global System
sections.screenshot_description_en: Cameron Macgregor explains the scale of the global energy crisis and key maritime choke points
sections.content_en:
The host recalls news of the sharp rise in oil and gas prices and asks what geopolitical and economic consequences should be expected. Macgregor breaks the consequences down into three points.

**The first is the energy crisis.** At the very least, he says, the world is in a global energy crisis that has already begun. He believes that it will very likely turn into a global recession or depression. He particularly highlights Asia's dependence on the flow not only of oil but also of liquefied natural gas, petrochemicals, and fertilizers, as well as on global trade. All that traffic does not only pass through the **Strait of Hormuz**, but also through the **Suez Canal**, the **Red Sea**, and other narrow passages along the edge of the war spreading across the Middle East.

The crisis, the guest estimates, affects between a fifth and a third of the global energy system and cannot be easily resolved. If the war ends quickly, it could last months, and if it does not end, years.

**The second point is the fragility of Western economies.** The economies of Western Europe and the US, says Macgregor, are already teetering on the brink of a major crisis. By that, he means several simultaneous crises:

- **a debt crisis** in the US and Western Europe,
- **a cost of living crisis**,
- **a breakdown of social cohesion**.

The guest attributes the breakdown of cohesion to the fact that Western countries, as he claims, are "flooded with millions of people" who live on state redistribution and whose existential minimum is subsidized by governments running out of money. The war, he believes, will accelerate this fragility. A financial crisis is possible, followed by a kind of economic depression in Western Europe and the US. One could say, he adds, that this process has already begun.

sections.subtitle: Kraj dolarskog sustava kao pozitivna vijest
sections.screenshot_description: Gost proglašava kraj unipolarnog trenutka i dolarskog sustava
sections.content:
Treću posljedicu Macgregor naziva pozitivnim razvojem. **Unipolarni trenutak, dolarski i eurodolarski sustav su gotovi**, kaže, a ovaj će ih rat i formalno okončati.

Dobrom viješću smatra pomak monetarne i ekonomske moći sa Zapada na Istok tijekom posljednjih dvadeset godina. Zbog tog pomaka globalni opskrbni lanci i industrija više nisu usredotočeni na Zapad, nego na Rusiju, Kinu, Indiju i slične zemlje. One su, po gostu, spremne prebroditi oluju, izgraditi nove monetarne sustave te alternativne trgovinske rute i odnose izvan Zapada. Kriza će taj proces ubrzati i ojačati, što Macgregor vidi kao vrlo dobru stvar za svijet.

Krajolik ekonomske moći sada je, ističe, naklonjen **globalnom Jugu**, odnosno „globalnoj većini“, a ostatak svijeta „dovodi se u red“. Kriza postoji, priznaje gost, ali s druge strane vidi uravnoteženiji i vjerojatno stabilniji svijet.
sections.subtitle_en: The End of the Dollar System as Positive News
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest proclaims the end of the unipolar moment and the dollar system
sections.content_en:
Macgregor calls the third consequence a positive development. **The unipolar moment, the dollar and Eurodollar systems are over**, he says, and this war will also formally end them.

He considers the shift of monetary and economic power from the West to the East over the last twenty years to be good news. Because of that shift, global supply chains and industry are no longer focused on the West, but on Russia, China, India, and similar countries. They are, according to the guest, ready to weather the storm, build new monetary systems, and alternative trade routes and relationships outside the West. The crisis will accelerate and strengthen that process, which Macgregor sees as a very good thing for the world.

The landscape of economic power is now, he points out, favorable to the **Global South**, that is, the "global majority," and the rest of the world is "getting its act together." A crisis exists, the guest admits, but on the other hand he sees a more balanced and probably more stable world.

sections.subtitle: Ne kraj Zapada, nego svijet koji je odrastao
sections.screenshot_description: Cameron Macgregor odgovara na tezu o kraju 500 godina zapadne hegemonije
sections.content:
Voditelj navodi da mnogi relevantni komentatori govore o kraju zapadne dominacije, odnosno o kraju **500 godina zapadne hegemonije**, te pita dijeli li gost to mišljenje.

Macgregor se ne slaže sasvim s tom formulacijom jer je, kaže, 500 godina dugo razdoblje. On radije kaže da je **ostatak svijeta odrastao**. Prema njemu, svjedočimo kraju svijeta nastalog nakon Drugoga svjetskog rata, svijeta koji je, tvrdi, „oštetio cijeli svijet“. Pritom misli na institucije iz Bretton Woodsa, međunarodna tijela za atomsku energiju i ostale strukture koje su nastale pod kišobranom američke dominacije.

Nije stvar samo u tome da su SAD oslabile ili da su pale pod utjecaj, kako kaže, vrlo destruktivnih lobija i nesposobnog upravljanja. Ostatak svijeta poručuje: „I mi smo velike sile i želimo sudjelovati u globalnom upravljanju.“

Zato gost očekuje **ponovno rođenje i reinvenciju zapadne civilizacije**, a ne nužno njezino uništenje. Taj će se proces odvijati u uravnoteženijem, multipolarnom svijetu u kojem bi pokretač industrije i najdinamičnija zemlja mogla biti Kina, a ne SAD. Obje stvari mogu biti istinite, kaže Macgregor. Zapad više nije neprikosnoveno središte svjetske civilizacije, što će ovaj sukob jasno pokazati, ali to nije ni kraj Zapada. Zapad se mora reorganizirati i prihvatiti da je ostatak svijeta prerastao unipolarni trenutak koji traje od kraja Drugoga svjetskog rata.

Gost vjeruje da zapadno stanovništvo „na ulici“ takvu promjenu želi i vjerojatno je pozdravlja. Protiv nje se, tvrdi, bore elite i tehnokrati. Kad oni odu, svijet će biti stabilniji.
sections.subtitle_en: Not the End of the West, but a World That Has Grown Up
sections.screenshot_description_en: Cameron Macgregor responds to the thesis about the end of 500 years of Western hegemony
sections.content_en:
The host notes that many relevant commentators talk about the end of Western dominance, that is, about the end of **500 years of Western hegemony**, and asks whether the guest shares that opinion.

Macgregor does not entirely agree with that formulation because, he says, 500 years is a long period. He prefers to say that **the rest of the world has grown up**. According to him, we are witnessing the end of the world created after the Second World War, a world that, he claims, has "damaged the entire world." In doing so, he refers to the Bretton Woods institutions, international atomic energy bodies, and other structures that emerged under the umbrella of American dominance.

It is not just that the US has weakened or that it has fallen under the influence of, as he says, very destructive lobbies and incompetent governance. The rest of the world is saying: "We are great powers too, and we want to participate in global governance."

Therefore, the guest expects **a rebirth and reinvention of Western civilization**, and not necessarily its destruction. That process will unfold in a more balanced, multipolar world in which the driver of industry and the most dynamic country could be China, not the US. Both things can be true, says Macgregor. The West is no longer the undisputed center of world civilization, which this conflict will clearly show, but that is not the end of the West either. The West must reorganize itself and accept that the rest of the world has outgrown the unipolar moment that has lasted since the end of the Second World War.

The guest believes that the Western population "on the street" wants such a change and probably welcomes it. Fighting against it, he claims, are the elites and technocrats. When they leave, the world will be more stable.

sections.subtitle: Duhovni rat: civilizacija zarobljena u materijalizmu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj citira gostov tekst o duhovnom ratu, a Macgregor objašnjava pojam demonske opsjednutosti Zapada
sections.content:
Voditelj se poziva na Macgregorov tekst i citira rečenicu koju je ondje pročitao: riječ je o „duhovnom ratu za egzorcizam zapadne civilizacije opsjednute demonskim silama“. Pita kako to treba razumjeti.

Macgregor najprije želi ostaviti po strani teorije zavjere. Mnogi, kaže, govore o „bankarskoj klasi“ i sličnim temama, ali činjenica je da zapadni svijet prolazi kroz **krizu identiteta**. Takve krize, objašnjava, ljudi proživljavaju i u svakodnevnom životu. Netko postane žrtva ovisnosti ili pretilosti ili upadne u neku od mnogih izopačenosti, i to postaje svojevrsna demonska opsjednutost pojedinca. Upravo se to, prema gostu, dogodilo Sjedinjenim Državama. Postale su arogantne, promiskuitetne i materijalističke.

Te sile, ističe, odumiru. Zapadni svijet, prosječni Amerikanci, Nijemci i Francuzi, prepoznaju da je materijalizam koji je dominirao razmišljanjem i kulturom možda sto godina, a možda još od industrijske revolucije, došao kraju. Potrebni su novi odgovori i novo uravnoteženje.

U središtu tog uravnoteženja Macgregor vidi **duhovnost**, odnosno ponovno buđenje svijesti da su ljudi duhovna bića. „Nismo samo potrošači, nismo samo proizvođači, nismo samo materijalni akteri unutar globalne ekonomije“, kaže. Ljudi imaju moralnu i drugu odgovornost. Zato očekuje širok zaokret, odnosno promjenu režima na Zapadu, u kojoj će destruktivni predstavnici tih „demonskih sila“, kako ih naziva parazitskim elitama koje su i same podlegle poroku nauštrb vrline, biti pometeni.

Ni to, ponavlja, ne znači kraj zapadne civilizacije. Sve civilizacije prolaze kroz takva razdoblja. Rusi su imali „paklensko stoljeće“, a Kinezi dva stoljeća, možda i duže. Preživjeli su, iznova se izgradili, i sada je svijet, kaže gost, na njihovoj strani. Zapad mora učiniti isto: vratiti se osnovama i ponovno se probuditi za moralni kodeks koji je izgubio iz vida najmanje stotinu godina.
sections.subtitle_en: Spiritual War: A Civilization Trapped in Materialism
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host quotes the guest's text on spiritual war, and Macgregor explains the concept of demonic possession of the West
sections.content_en:
The host refers to Macgregor's text and quotes a sentence he read there: it is about a "spiritual war to exorcise Western civilization possessed by demonic forces." He asks how that should be understood.

Macgregor first wants to set conspiracy theories aside. Many, he says, talk about the "banking class" and similar topics, but the fact is that the Western world is undergoing an **identity crisis**. Such crises, he explains, people experience in everyday life as well. Someone falls victim to addiction or obesity or falls into one of many depravities, and that becomes a kind of demonic possession of the individual. Precisely that, according to the guest, happened to the United States. They have become arrogant, promiscuous, and materialistic.

Those forces, he points out, are dying out. The Western world, average Americans, Germans, and Frenchmen, recognize that the materialism that dominated thought and culture for perhaps a hundred years, and perhaps ever since the Industrial Revolution, has come to an end. New answers and a new balancing are needed.

At the center of that balancing, Macgregor sees **spirituality**, that is, a reawakening of the awareness that humans are spiritual beings. "We are not just consumers, we are not just producers, we are not just material actors within the global economy," he says. Humans have moral and other responsibilities. Therefore, he expects a broad turn, that is, regime change in the West, in which the destructive representatives of those "demonic forces," as he calls the parasitic elites who themselves succumbed to vice at the expense of virtue, will be swept away.

Even that, he repeats, does not mean the end of Western civilization. All civilizations go through such periods. The Russians had a "hellish century," and the Chinese two centuries, perhaps even longer. They survived, rebuilt themselves, and now the world, says the guest, is on their side. The West must do the same: return to basics and reawaken to the moral code that it has lost sight of for at least a hundred years.

sections.subtitle: Vrijeme pročišćenja i vjera u obične ljude
sections.screenshot_description: Gost potvrđuje voditeljev zaključak o vremenu geopolitičkog, ekonomskog i duhovnog pročišćenja
sections.content:
Voditelj sažima dosadašnji razgovor: vrijeme je za promjenu, a ovo je razdoblje **pročišćenja, geopolitičkog, ekonomskog, ali i duhovnog**. Macgregor se slaže: „Upravo tako.“

Čovječanstvo, kaže, na svim razinama sazrijeva i preobražava se, a središte tog procesa je Zapad. Zapadna kultura, ekonomski model i politički sustavi dugo su bili dominantni, a Zapad je dugo bio predvodnik ljudskih promjena. Sada se to mijenja i Zapad se mora prilagoditi.

Gost vjeruje da hoće jer ima povjerenja u obične ljude. Nabraja prosječne Nijemce, Čehe, Slovake i Poljake, a zatim dodaje i **Hrvate**. Bio je u svim tim zemljama i kaže da obični ljudi točno razumiju o čemu govori. Problem su, po njemu, ljudi u Bruxellesu, Washingtonu i New Yorku, od kojih su mnogi vrlo bogati, a, kako se oštro izražava, „nemaju pojma što se, dovraga, događa“.
sections.subtitle_en: A Time of Purification and Faith in Ordinary People
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest confirms the host's conclusion about a time of geopolitical, economic, and spiritual purification
sections.content_en:
The host summarizes the conversation so far: it is time for change, and this is a period of **purification, geopolitical, economic, but also spiritual**. Macgregor agrees: "Precisely so."

Humanity, he says, is maturing and transforming on all levels, and the center of that process is the West. Western culture, the economic model, and political systems have long been dominant, and the West has long been the leader of human change. Now that is changing, and the West must adapt.

The guest believes that it will, because he has confidence in ordinary people. He lists average Germans, Czechs, Slovaks, and Poles, and then also adds **Croats**. He has been to all those countries and says that ordinary people understand exactly what he is talking about. The problem, according to him, is the people in Brussels, Washington, and New York, many of whom are very wealthy, and, as he puts it sharply, "have no idea what the hell is going on."

> "Magisterium alignment: Catholic doctrine affirms the inherent dignity of the human person and the necessity of moral and spiritual renewal, but caution is warranted regarding fatalistic geopolitical determinism."

sections.subtitle: Svijet 2030.: regionalniji, multipolarni i bez NATO-a
sections.screenshot_description: Cameron Macgregor iznosi predviđanja za svijet do 2030. godine
sections.content:
Voditelj priznaje da je predviđanja uvijek teško davati, ali pita gosta kako vidi budućnost. Macgregor kaže da dosadašnje pretpostavke daju jasnu sliku.

Prvo, prema njegovoj ocjeni, SAD i Izrael izgubili su rat na Bliskom istoku. Za SAD je to bila **kobna pogreška**. Globalno vojno carstvo koje je Amerika gradila osamdeset godina, kaže, gotovo je, a gotova je i dominacija dolara.

Sve to znači krizu. Gost podsjeća da je kriza grčka riječ koja znači **izbor**, iako ljudi to zaboravljaju. Zapad sada bira vrlo drugačiji put, i to zato što mu je nametnut.

Do **2030.** svijet će, predviđa Macgregor, biti regionalniji i multipolarniji. To ne znači kraj globalizacije: zemlje će i dalje komunicirati i trgovati, ali svijet će biti uravnoteženiji i raspodijeljeniji. Zapad će vjerojatno dobiti nove oblike upravljanja. „EU je gotov, NATO je gotov“, kaže gost, a kraj je i američkog carstva u Europi. Očekuje zato novo povezivanje s Rusijom, Kinom i drugim dijelovima svijeta. „Samo će izgledati malo drugačije. Tamo idemo“, zaključuje.
sections.subtitle_en: The World of 2030: More Regional, Multipolar, and Without NATO
sections.screenshot_description_en: Cameron Macgregor presents predictions for the world by 2030
sections.content_en:
The host admits that predictions are always difficult to make, but asks the guest how he sees the future. Macgregor says that previous assumptions provide a clear picture.

First, according to his assessment, the US and Israel have lost the war in the Middle East. For the US, that was a **fatal mistake**. The global military empire that America built for eighty years, he says, is over, and the dominance of the dollar is over as well.

All of this means a crisis. The guest recalls that crisis is a Greek word meaning **choice**, although people forget that. The West is now choosing a very different path, and that is because it was imposed upon it.

By **2030**, the world will, Macgregor predicts, be more regional and more multipolar. That does not mean the end of globalization: countries will still communicate and trade, but the world will be more balanced and more distributed. The West will likely receive new forms of governance. "The EU is over, NATO is over," says the guest, and it is also the end of the American empire in Europe. He therefore expects a new reconnection with Russia, China, and other parts of the world. "It will just look a little different. That is where we are heading," he concludes.

sections.subtitle: Split, Hvar i Dioklecijan: zašto bi radije živio u Hrvatskoj nego u Grčkoj
sections.screenshot_description: Gost s oduševljenjem govori o posjetima Splitu, Hvaru i dalmatinskoj obali
sections.content:
Pred kraj razgovora voditelj pita gosta o svojoj domovini: kako mu se kao svjetskom putniku svidjela Hrvatska i koje je gradove posjetio.

Macgregor kaže da je bio u **Splitu** i na **Hvaru**. Hrvatska je, kaže, jedna od najljepših zemalja koje je posjetio, a do sada je, koliko se sjeća, obišao više od 35 zemalja. Posebno voli **dalmatinsku obalu**.

Split mu je drag i zbog povijesti. Grad je, napominje, bio mjesto u koje se nakon povlačenja s vlasti povukao **car Dioklecijan**. Hrvatska, dodaje, ima nevjerojatnu povijest koja počinje još s Grcima, a ostavili su traga i Mlečani i Austrijanci.

Ljudima, kaže, stalno govori da bi između Grčke i Hrvatske izabrao Hrvatsku. Voli grčku hranu, ali bi radije živio u Hrvatskoj, i to iz mnogo razloga. U Hrvatskoj je bio više puta, a u Splitu živi i njegov prijatelj, pa dolazi kad god može.
sections.subtitle_en: Split, Hvar, and Diocletian: Why He Would Rather Live in Croatia than in Greece
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks enthusiastically about visits to Split, Hvar, and the Dalmatian coast
sections.content_en:
Towards the end of the conversation, the host asks the guest about his homeland: how he, as a world traveler, liked Croatia and which cities he visited.

Macgregor says that he has been to **Split** and on **Hvar**. Croatia, he says, is one of the most beautiful countries he has visited, and so far, as far as he recalls, he has visited more than 35 countries. He particularly loves the **Dalmatian coast**.

Split is also dear to him because of history. The city, he notes, was the place where **Emperor Diocletian** retired after relinquishing power. Croatia, he adds, has an incredible history that begins as early as the Greeks, and the Venetians and Austrians have also left their mark.

To people, he says, he constantly says that between Greece and Croatia, he would choose Croatia. He loves Greek food, but would rather live in Croatia, and that for many reasons. He has been to Croatia several times, and his friend also lives in Split, so he comes whenever he can.

sections.subtitle: Završna poruka: Amerika će se probuditi
sections.screenshot_description: Cameron Macgregor upućuje završnu poruku slušateljima Mrežnice
sections.content:
Voditelj zahvaljuje gostu na vremenu i kaže da je uživao u razgovoru. Macgregor uzvraća da mu je drago razgovarati s publikom Mrežnice i upućuje završnu poruku.

Sjedinjene Države trenutačno prolaze kroz **tranziciju**, kaže, ali će je, kao i sva carstva, preživjeti i krenuti dalje. Svaku naciju, ističe, određuju njezini ljudi, bilo da je riječ o Hrvatskoj, Srbiji ili Rusiji. Ameriku određuju ljudi poput njega i njegovih predaka koji su stigli prije četiri stotine godina.

„Još smo ovdje. Probudit ćemo se“, poručuje Macgregor. Dodaje da ovo nije kraj svijeta i da će s druge strane ove krize svijet biti mnogo bolji.

Voditelj gostu i njegovoj obitelji želi sve najbolje, a Macgregor uzvraća istim željama. Razgovor završava pozdravom „Bye-bye“.
sections.subtitle_en: Final Message: America Will Wake Up
sections.screenshot_description_en: Cameron Macgregor delivers a closing message to the listeners of Mrežnica
sections.content_en:
The host thanks the guest for his time and says he enjoyed the conversation. Macgregor responds that he is glad to speak with the audience of Mrežnica and delivers a final message.

The United States is currently going through a **transition**, he says, but will, like all empires, survive it and move on. Every nation, he points out, is defined by its people, whether it is Croatia, Serbia, or Russia. America is defined by people like him and his ancestors who arrived four hundred years ago.

"We are still here. We will wake up," Macgregor conveys. He adds that this is not the end of the world and that on the other side of this crisis the world will be much better.

The host wishes the guest and his family all the best, and Macgregor returns the same wishes. The conversation ends with the greeting "Bye-bye."
